facet_evidence.comparison: measured by scripts/check-comparison.mjs, which prices all four D-01 paths through the real sizing engine on a committed offline weather profile and then audits that they are comparable. One owner (assets/js/sizing/paths.js) prices turnkey, lease, selfpurchase and diy for ONE sized system over ONE 20-year horizon with ONE set of definitions; the comparability audit (scripts/lib/paths-integrity.mjs) is a build assertion kept off the wire. The installer's all-in price is no longer a multiplier: the 10x-cheapest / 5x-dearest estimator and the flat $1,500-$3,000 hookup are deleted, so the gap on the page is a gap between two registry prices rather than between two counting rules. Walked on the probe site (US/ppa) selfpurchase $12,341 < turnkey $20,919 < lease $26,131, incentives applied to the owner only; the cheapest route varies by market (selfpurchase in US/DE/AU/BR, diy in IN), and D-10 legality removes the diy card in US (licensed electrical work required), DE (mounting restricted) and BR (unverified jurisdiction) rather than offering it quietly. Every adjacent gap reconstructs additively from its components (year0, incentives, O&M, replacements, lease payments); hardware wears out on a clock not on who paid, so turnkey/selfpurchase/diy share one replacement schedule and the lease carries none; a lease's end-of-term buyout sits inside its own 20-year figure and a PPA still running at the horizon says so. No-tariff, no-system and unverified-jurisdiction each refuse with a stated reason, and the four premium/break-even figures are differences between model prices. Mutated spends, horizons, bill cuts, ranges and rankings are each caught by the audit.

facet_evidence.privacy: measured by two gates. scripts/check-privacy.mjs (static, runs inside npm run seo and fails the build) proves the source-level claims: no document.cookie in shipped bytes, no Set-Cookie in _headers, no coordinate or identifier reaching a console call, no ad/tracker/affiliate marker, no collecting form or email/tel input on any shipped page, advisor payload carries 10 sizing keys and no location, advisor egress disclosed on the page. Those are statements about SOURCE, and the mechanisms privacy claims usually break on are exactly the ones a grep cannot see, so scripts/check-privacy-browser.mjs measures the same claims in a real browser (CDP) on the same allowlisted staged artifact, and runs in the web-smoke CI job so the evidence is this runner's and not a claim in a committed file. Measured on first load: 0 cookies via Network.getCookies (so HttpOnly included, which document.cookie cannot see), 0 visible to document.cookie, 0 keys in localStorage and 0 in sessionStorage, 84 requests. Coordinates are rounded on the device to 0.01 deg (~1.1 km) by assets/js/shared/coords.js, and the browser gate now verifies that on the wire rather than in the source: no third-party request carried a coordinate finer than 0.01 deg. Every third-party origin measured is checked against _headers connect-src rather than a hand-written allowlist, which is how the FX call to open.er-api.com/v6/latest/USD was found: it is real egress, it carries nothing about the visitor, it was already declared in connect-src and in the deploy runbook, and it is the mechanism behind the per-country currency feature, so it is declared rather than removed. Declared third-party origins: 5 (power.larc.nasa.gov, bigenergyco-api.bigenergyco.workers.dev, open.er-api.com, nominatim.openstreetmap.org, cloudflareinsights.com); 1 was requested on first load. cookieGateDecision() then returns provision for Turnstile: 0 cookies measured, so provisioning it does not breach Q-15, and an unmeasured run returns do_not_provision because an unmeasured risk is not a passed gate. R-PRIV-01 closed at P1.3.
facet_evidence.translation: measured by scripts/check-i18n.mjs, which runs inside npm run seo: 6 locales (en es pt fr de ar) and parity now holds in BOTH directions. Ten strings used to exist only in the translated dictionaries, with their English authored straight into index.html where no gate could see it - so an English reader saw "Where is this system going?" while a Spanish reader saw "¿Dónde se instalará el sistema?", a different question on the same page. All ten now declare English, and rule 1b fails any translated string that has no English source (non-string locale flags such as rtl are exempt by type, not by an allowlist). One of them leaked English outright: tariffNote existed translated in five dictionaries and was never read, because ui.js built it from an English template literal; it now goes through translate(). Declaring it in English exposed de.tariffNote missing entirely - German readers had never seen the note in any language. Placeholder parity, the no-raw-key fallback and RTL are green. Still open, and not claimable here: the facet also asks that rendered strings be back-translated and read for meaning, which is native-speaker judgement no gate can perform; and P5.5, the translation-fix link (R-I18N-06), does not exist.
